o1.biggest_strength: It nails every signal in the data — Simplify debts split out, the 4,900 no-click searches, the 2,000 Apple/Google refunds — and turns them into three publish-ready articles plus a ticket forecast with real working and a down-side range.
o1.biggest_mistake: It still tells people to turn Simplify debts off to see who owes whom, which changes the view for the whole group and risks new confusion; a safer article would show the per-expense view without flipping the group setting.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Drop the group-wide Simplify toggle advice in favour of a per-expense view, and confirm the in-app button names before publishing so the steps are exactly right.

o2.biggest_strength: It reads fastest of the two — bad news in three lines, a tight priority table, articles that answer in the first sentence, and a transparent 25%–50% range with the maths shown.
o2.biggest_mistake: It says 'you can restore deleted expenses from Activity' as fact without telling people to check that the Restore option exists on their version, and its 'Contact us' fallbacks lean on a form the owner may not have wired up.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add the web version of the restore steps and a one-line check that the bold button names match the live app, so the articles are genuinely publish-ready.

reason: Both are strong and correctly ranked, but Output 2 is faster to read, states the bad news first, gives an honest range, and its articles are cleaner and more findable — the owner would pay for it.
